parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no birth-sex facility ban, no documented border document friction or police targeting of trans people; expression is lawful and visibility is high (3,000-person trans march, large Pride). The severe surgery-gated ID-marker rule is resident-facing machinery a visitor never uses — its documents come from home — so it counts only as a climate signal of lagging institutional recognition, not a visitor exposure. Visitor-facing negatives are real but sub-tier-1: 17% of reported discrimination occurring in restrooms/changing rooms and most all-gender toilets failing standards is facilities friction, not exclusion; rising anti-gender politics, a 'two genders' party position and the 2018 referendum show contested social climate, and no working visitor-facing accommodation remedy is documented. No violence data at all, which in a well-documented state is mildly positive. Sits between the 0.65 (lawful, friction, uneven remedy) and 0.75 anchors; the open questions and unresolved appeal keep it at 0.65 rather than higher.
